name: hue
description: Every workspace folder gets its own color, and the window follows the folder you work in. Warns on production folders and protected branches.

commands.title: Save (asks first in a PROD place)

hue.folders.markdownDescription: Workspace folder name → color: `red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `teal`, `blue`, `purple`, `pink` or `#rrggbb`. Only applies in a `.code-workspace`, which is where the colors are written.

hue.auto.description: Give a folder with no color of its own a stable one picked from its name.

hue.colors.markdownDescription: Named colors, added to or replacing the defaults (`red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `teal`, `blue`, `purple`, `pink`). A value is a hue (0-360) or `#rrggbb`: `{ "blue": "#3b82f6", "brand": 300 }`. Used by `hue.folders` and the automatic color.

hue.parts.description: Which parts of the window are tinted.

hue.danger.description: Dangerous (production) places: a folder name (all of it) or `folder/path` (that path, `*` and `**` allowed). While the active file is in one, the title bar is red and the status bar shows PROD.

hue.dangerReadonly.markdownDescription: Open the `hue.danger` places read-only (Hue adds them to the workspace's `files.readonlyInclude`), which also stops saves from the menu and auto save. Make a file writable for the session with **File: Set Active Editor Writeable in Session**.

hue.protectedBranches.description: The status bar turns amber while the active folder's repository is on one of these branches. Empty to turn it off.

hue.enabled.description: Turn the whole extension off for this workspace: its colors are removed.
